A later police inquiry found fraud-linked receipts in his account, creating a valuable unresolved question of whether he was a knowing participant or a socially engineered mule.
cases.research_notes: Only the petitioner's INR 1,000 outgoing payment is coded as his focal loss. INR 12,800 in a third-party complaint and INR 147,599/2,000 found in account layers are fraud-linked flows, not his personal loss. cases.case_title: Nadiad sexual-lure and fake Crime Branch extortion
cases.impersonated_identity_detail: Local Crime Branch police officials
cases.initial_contact_summary: On 4 January 2010, a woman asked the complainant for a lift while he was travelling from Ahmedabad toward Nadiad and later proposed an intimate encounter at a secluded location.
cases.pretext_summary: After the complainant reached the secluded place, four men arrived and falsely posed as Local Crime Branch police officials, accused him of a sexual offence, beat him and demanded money as a purported settlement.
cases.other_psychological_mechanism: Sexual lure followed by police-authority impersonation and threat of criminal accusation.
cases.requested_action: Pay INR 50,000 as a purported settlement to avoid being booked for a sexual offence.
cases.victim_action: The complainant surrendered INR 300, his mobile phone and a copy of his driving licence and was being taken toward Ahmedabad to obtain the remaining demanded money when genuine police intercepted the car.
cases.other_evidence: Victim testimony; genuine police interception; recovered cash, driving-licence copy, mobile phones and vehicle; medical evidence of injuries.
cases.attribution_target: Male police-impersonation and extortion operators, with the alleged role of the female lure actor assessed separately.
cases.attribution_limitations: The appellate court found the complainant and police evidence sufficient against the male police-impersonation actors but held that the prosecution did not prove the female accused's prior association or common intention with them.
cases.alternative_explanation: The female accused's presence and sexual proposal did not, by themselves, prove that she was part of the extortion conspiracy; the appellate court gave her the benefit of doubt on that linkage.
cases.primary_evidentiary_gap: Direct evidence establishing whether the female lure actor coordinated with the male police-impersonation group before the incident.
cases.legal_provisions: IPC 170; IPC 419; IPC 395; IPC 114; FIR also invoked IPC 386
cases.disposition: The Gujarat High Court upheld the core factual finding that male accused falsely posed as Crime Branch police officials and extorted the complainant, while finding the evidence insufficient to connect the female accused to the common plan and acquitting her of the relevant charges.
cases.case_summary: A motorcyclist travelling toward Nadiad accepted a woman's request for a lift and later agreed to an intimate encounter at a secluded place. Four men then arrived in a car, falsely presented themselves as Local Crime Branch officers, assaulted him, threatened prosecution for a sexual offence and demanded INR 50,000 as a settlement. They took INR 300, his phone and a copy of his driving licence and were transporting him toward Ahmedabad to obtain more money when genuine police stopped the car. The later Gujarat High Court judgment treated the police-impersonation extortion as proved against the relevant male accused but found the evidence insufficient to establish that the woman was part of their pre-arranged common plan.
cases.research_notes: Exact incident date is expressly stated in the appellate judgment. The focal loss field records the INR 300 actually taken, not the larger INR 50,000 demand. Actor coding separates the proved male police-impersonation conduct from the weaker attribution of the female lure actor.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Victim testimony, police interception and appellate findings directly support the impersonation, threats and taking of property.
actors.conduct_assessed: Posing as Local Crime Branch officers, threatening a sexual-offence case, assaulting the complainant and demanding a settlement payment.
actors.attribution_limitations: The record strongly supports the conduct of the relevant male accused but does not imply that every person present had the same role.
actors.alternative_explanation: Individual responsibility remains accused-specific within the group.
actors.relationship_note: Separate from the female lure actor because the appellate court treated her alleged coordination differently.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The source supports the request for a lift and sexual proposal, but the appellate court found no sufficient proof that she had pre-arranged the later extortion with the male accused.
actors.conduct_assessed: Requesting a lift and proposing an intimate encounter that preceded the police-impersonation extortion.
actors.attribution_limitations: The appellate court found insufficient evidence of prior association, common intention or conspiracy with the male extortion actors.
actors.alternative_explanation: Her conduct may have been independent rather than part of the extortion plan.
actors.relationship_note: Do not infer conspiracy merely from the temporal sequence.

cases.case_summary: A Goan woman received a Facebook friend request in August 2020 from a profile using the fictitious name Steve Jose and claiming to be a UK national. After building an online friendship, the persona said he would send her a birthday gift from abroad. The victim then received calls claiming to come from customs officials in Delhi and was pressured to pay charges, with the persona saying the money spent on the gift would otherwise be lost. She deposited about INR 5 lakh into supplied accounts. cases.case_title: ICICI phishing email and disputed IP/device attribution
cases.court_or_authority: I Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore
cases.impersonated_identity_detail: ICICI Bank account-update communication
cases.initial_contact_summary: The prosecution alleged that an ICICI Bank-branded phishing email induced the NRI account holder to provide login particulars under an account-update pretext.
cases.pretext_summary: A sender presented the message as an ICICI Bank communication requiring account details to be updated, after which unauthorized access and transfers were alleged.
cases.requested_action: Provide ICICI Bank login particulars in response to the purported account-update communication.
cases.victim_action: The source states that the account holder furnished login particulars and INR 400,000 was then transferred from the account to two beneficiary accounts.
cases.other_evidence: Truth Lab forensic report, domain-name lookup material, pay-in slips, cheque material and seizure records.
cases.attribution_target: Nikhil Dhingra and Saupam Das as the alleged phishing and unauthorized-account-access operators
cases.attribution_limitations: The phishing-email IP differed from the transaction IP; the accused-linked IP was not shown to conduct the transactions; the victim and complainant were not examined; seizure proof was deficient; and the Truth Lab report found no phishing, transaction or inter-accused communication material on the examined laptop.
cases.alternative_explanation: The named beneficiary-account holders or other unresolved operators may have controlled the phishing or transaction path; the source does not establish overlap between those roles and the two tried accused.
cases.primary_evidentiary_gap: Authenticated end-to-end linkage from the phishing email, login session and transaction IPs to identified human operators, together with a completed beneficiary-account investigation.
cases.legal_provisions: IT Act 66C; IT Act 66D; IPC 417; IPC 34
cases.disposition: Accused Nos.1 and 2 were acquitted on 6 March 2015; the original file was preserved because split-up proceedings against accused Nos.3 to 5 remained pending.
cases.case_summary: A prosecution alleged that an ICICI Bank phishing email induced an NRI account holder to disclose login particulars, after which INR 400,000 was transferred to two Kolkata beneficiary accounts. The final trial judgment acquitted the two accused before the court. The court emphasized mismatched phishing and transaction IP evidence, non-examination of the victim and complainant, deficient seizure proof, incomplete beneficiary investigation and a Truth Lab report that found no phishing or transaction material on the seized laptop. The incident is therefore coded as a clear phishing sequence with unresolved human attribution.
cases.research_notes: The judgment header lists 22 April 2009 as the date of offence, while the reasons identify the illegal transactions as occurring on 17 and 18 April 2009 and describe the complaint as filed on 22 April. The structured incident dates use the more specific transaction dates stated in the reasons. Four transaction-related IP addresses were reported as belonging to the USA, so cross_border_dimension is coded suspected rather than yes.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The prosecution and exhibits reconstruct a phishing email impersonating ICICI Bank, but the final judgment does not resolve the human sender.

actors.attribution_limitations: The source documents the phishing communication but the relevant IP trail did not resolve the human sender and did not establish that either tried accused sent it.
actors.alternative_explanation: The sender may have been an unresolved third party distinct from the tried accused and beneficiary-account holders.

actors.attribution_limitations: The accused-linked IP was not shown to conduct the transactions; the phishing and transaction IPs differed; no incriminating material was seized from him; and the trial ended in acquittal.
actors.alternative_explanation: The source leaves open that another person controlled the phishing infrastructure.
actors.relationship_note: Identified human, but identity resolution is not a finding that the alleged phishing conduct was proved.

cases.case_title: Duplicate-SIM takeover and unresolved OTP-transfer attribution
cases.court_or_authority: XLV Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru
cases.impersonated_identity_detail: Legitimate mobile subscriber whose registered number was taken over through a duplicate SIM
cases.reconnaissance_description: The attack required use of the complainant's specific mobile number, but the source does not explain how that information was obtained.
cases.initial_contact_summary: On 10 May 2017 an unknown person caused the complainant's mobile number to be locked and a duplicate SIM to be obtained; the exact telecom-facing contact channel is not reported.
cases.pretext_summary: The unknown requester allegedly assumed authority over the legitimate subscriber number, enabling receipt of OTPs and subsequent unauthorized bank transfers.
cases.other_psychological_mechanism: Subscriber-identity substitution at the telecom-service layer.
cases.requested_action: Issue or activate a duplicate SIM for the complainant's registered mobile number.
cases.victim_action: The telecom service replaced the SIM; the complainant later discovered that money had been transferred from his bank account. The complainant did not knowingly comply with the attacker.
cases.other_evidence: A Vivo mobile and purse were seized; an FSL acknowledgment was marked, but the forensic report itself was unavailable at trial.
cases.attribution_target: Harish S.R. as the alleged duplicate-SIM and OTP-transfer operator
cases.attribution_limitations: The complainant had never seen the accused before court; the seizure pancha did not support the prosecution; ownership of the seized mobile was not established; the FSL report was unavailable; and investigators did not establish the transfer amount or ownership of the recipient account.
cases.alternative_explanation: The duplicate-SIM requester, seized-device user and bank-transfer operator may have been different persons, and the trial record did not establish that Harish S.R. performed those functions.
cases.primary_evidentiary_gap: Telecom replacement records, completed forensic results and bank-account evidence linking the duplicate SIM, OTP use and recipient account to an identified human operator.
cases.legal_provisions: IT Act 66C; IT Act 66D; IPC 419; IPC 420
cases.disposition: Harish S.R. was acquitted on 28 March 2026. The court highlighted hostile/weak witness evidence, missing forensic results and failures to establish device and recipient-account ownership.
cases.case_summary: The complainant reported that his mobile number was locked, a duplicate SIM was obtained and OTP access was then used to transfer money from his bank account. Harish S.R. was prosecuted as the alleged operator. At trial the complainant said he had never seen the accused before court, the seizure witness did not support the prosecution, the seized phone's ownership was not established, the FSL report was unavailable and the transfer amount and recipient-account owner had not been investigated. The final judgment acquitted the accused, making the case a clear example of a visible SIM-takeover mechanism without resolved human attribution.
cases.research_notes: No financial_loss_inr is coded because the final judgment does not state a reliable transfer amount. The source identifies a 10 to 16 May 2017 offence period.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The complainant's evidence supports that the registered SIM was replaced without his authority, but the human requester is not resolved.

actors.alternative_explanation: The requester and the later OTP/banking operator may have been different persons.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The source records use of OTP access followed by transfer from the complainant's bank account, but investigators did not establish the recipient account owner.

actors.attribution_limitations: The amount, recipient-account owner and human banking-session operator were not established in the final trial record.
actors.alternative_explanation: The financial operator may have been distinct from the duplicate-SIM requester and from Harish S.R.
actors.relationship_note: Financial layer kept separate from telecom impersonation.

cases.case_title: Lead Management service impersonation and card/app fraud
cases.court_or_authority: VIII Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City
cases.platform_primary: In-person / mobile apps / credit and debit cards
cases.impersonated_identity_detail: Purported employees of a Lead Management System company offering transport and courier business leads
cases.initial_contact_summary: Two men came to Mayur Angadi's transport office claiming to work for a lead-management company that could provide transport and courier business opportunities.
cases.pretext_summary: The visitors said a small INR 200 registration or service payment had to be made by card, took the complainant's phone and cards, downloaded applications and represented failed card swipes as part of the service process.
cases.other_psychological_mechanism: Business-opportunity pretext combined with a nominal registration/payment step.
cases.requested_action: Allow the purported service employees to access the mobile phone, install applications and process a nominal INR 200 card payment.
cases.victim_action: The complainant handed over his phone, allowed applications to be installed and provided a Citibank credit card and SBI debit card for swiping. The next day he received debit messages totalling INR 63,000.
cases.other_evidence: SBI and credit-card statements, complaint, victim testimony and voluntary statements; the relevant phones, wallet/application records and beneficiary evidence were not secured.
cases.attribution_target: Rakesh Kumar K.A. and Raghavendra @ Raghu as the alleged in-person, card and app operators
cases.attribution_limitations: The complaint did not name or describe the accused, no CCTV existed, the complainant's phone and the accused phones were not seized, app/wallet evidence and IP/network evidence were not collected, and no transfer to the accused or a known associate was proved.
cases.alternative_explanation: The in-person visitors and the unknown operator responsible for the later unauthorized card/account transactions may not have been the same persons; the financial endpoint was unresolved.
cases.primary_evidentiary_gap: Device/app logs, card/wallet transaction provenance and beneficiary records linking the in-person visitors to the unauthorized INR 63,000 transactions.
cases.legal_provisions: IPC 419; IPC 420; IPC 34; IT Act 66C; IT Act 66D
cases.disposition: Rakesh Kumar K.A. and Raghavendra @ Raghu were acquitted on 18 July 2025 after the court found the prosecution had not connected the visitors, apps, card details, OTP path or transaction proceeds to them with cogent evidence.
cases.case_summary: Two men allegedly entered a Bengaluru transport business claiming to represent a lead-management company, offered business leads, took the complainant's phone, downloaded applications and insisted that a nominal INR 200 payment be made by card. The complainant later saw four unauthorized debits totalling INR 63,000. Although bank and card statements were produced, investigators did not seize the relevant phones, obtain app or wallet evidence, trace IP or communication records, or prove that the proceeds reached the accused or their associates. The final trial judgment acquitted both accused.
cases.research_notes: The source gives the incident as 17/18 September 2018. financial_loss_inr records the four victim-reported debits totalling INR 63,000. The payment_method is coded card because the source ties the attack to the complainant's credit/debit cards, while the precise downstream wallet or online settlement path remained unproved.

cases.case_title: Fake Facebook romance persona and INR 14 lakh transfer allegation
cases.court_or_authority: I Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru
cases.impersonated_identity_detail: Syedaliya.mujasim Facebook persona using fake photographs and a claimed romantic relationship
cases.reconnaissance_description: The fake profile directly targeted the complainant with a friend request; no distinct pre-contact reconnaissance stage is established.
cases.initial_contact_summary: The prosecution alleged that a Facebook account in the name Syedaliya.mujasim, using fake photographs, sent Mohammed Waseem Ahamed a friend request and began chatting with him.
cases.pretext_summary: The persona allegedly cultivated a romantic relationship, said she was in love with the complainant and later requested money for educational and other expenses.
cases.other_psychological_mechanism: Romantic trust-building through a fake social-media persona, followed by an alleged threat when the complainant challenged the scheme.
cases.requested_action: Transfer money to accounts supplied during the purported romantic relationship.
cases.victim_action: The complainant testified that he transferred a total of INR 1,400,000 on repeated requests, though the final court found the bank records did not corroborate the alleged transfer chain to accused No.2.
cases.other_evidence: Indian Bank account extract, alleged ATM-card seizure, CCTV footage of an alleged withdrawal, CDR material concerning accused No.1 and victim testimony.
cases.attribution_target: Harshiya Khanam and Sherkhan as the alleged operators of the fake Facebook romance and payment scheme
cases.attribution_limitations: The final trial concerned accused No.2 Harshiya Khanam while the case against accused No.1 Sherkhan had been split up. The bank extracts did not corroborate the complainant's claimed deposits to accused No.2, no CDR linked accused No.2 to the victim calls, the CCTV footage was not proved in accordance with law, and investigators did not obtain Facebook account records.
cases.alternative_explanation: The fake Facebook persona, callers, recipient-account controllers and ATM withdrawal actor may have been different people; the final source did not establish that Harshiya Khanam performed those functions.
cases.primary_evidentiary_gap: Facebook provider/login records, CDR evidence for the alleged caller, authenticated CCTV material and a transaction-by-transaction bank trail linking the complainant's payments to specific operators.
cases.disposition: Harshiya Khanam was acquitted on 16 March 2021. Proceedings against accused No.1 Sherkhan had earlier been split into C.C.No.6519/2021.
cases.case_summary: The prosecution alleged that a fake Facebook profile called Syedaliya.mujasim used false photographs, befriended Mohammed Waseem Ahamed and cultivated a romantic relationship before requesting money for educational and other expenses. The complainant said he transferred INR 1,400,000 to several accounts and was later threatened when he questioned the scheme. In the final trial of accused No.2 Harshiya Khanam, the court found the documentary evidence did not corroborate the claimed transfer and communication links: no relevant CDR connected her to the calls, Facebook records had not been investigated, bank extracts did not show the alleged deposits to her account, and CCTV evidence was not proved in accordance with law. She was acquitted.
cases.research_notes: The judgment header gives the offence period as 1 March 2012 to 18 February 2013, but the prosecution narrative separately records an alleged threat on 18 December 2013. The Atlas therefore uses 1 March 2012 to 18 December 2013 as the broad source-supported incident interval. INR 1,400,000 is coded as the complainant/prosecution-reported focal loss, with the court's non-corroboration preserved explicitly.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The complaint and charge-sheet narrative reconstruct a fake Facebook profile using false photographs and a romantic pretext, but the final trial does not resolve the human operator.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the fake Facebook persona, cultivating romantic trust and requesting money.
actors.attribution_limitations: Investigators did not obtain or prove Facebook provider/account records, so the human behind the persona remained unresolved.
actors.alternative_explanation: The persona may have been operated by accused No.1, accused No.2 or another participant; the final record does not establish which.

cases.court_or_authority: XLV Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru
cases.platform_primary: Business onboarding / internal email approval / bank refund workflow
cases.impersonated_identity_detail: S.N. Finance Limited Services, presented as a legitimate motor-broking and insurance-lead entity
cases.initial_contact_summary: A fictitious entity presented as S.N. Finance Limited Services approached ICICI Lombard for insurance-lead business and a cash-depository arrangement.
cases.pretext_summary: The entity was presented as a legitimate motor-broking business. The judgment further records fake internal email approvals used in refund processing, after which large sums were routed to the associated HDFC account.
cases.requested_action: Create and use a cash-depository relationship for the purported business entity and process refunds under apparently valid internal approvals.
cases.victim_action: The company onboarded the entity and processed refunds into the associated account; the prosecution alleged refunds totalling INR 88,983,100.
cases.other_evidence: Bank statements and KYC records, internal enquiry material, seizure/search records, undertaking affidavit and a Section 65B certificate.
cases.attribution_target: Anubhava Sharma as the accused found guilty of cheating and cheating by personation
cases.attribution_limitations: The judgment is internally inconsistent: its header says the accused is acquitted, while the operative order convicts under IPC 420 and IT Act 66D. The undertaking reproduced in the judgment also contains dates later than the stated judgment date, and the exact operational role of each participant is not fully resolved.
cases.alternative_explanation: Different people may have handled the external fictitious entity, internal email approvals and downstream receipt of funds; the final judgment does not map every operational act to the accused.
cases.primary_evidentiary_gap: A clean actor-by-actor mapping between fictitious-entity creation, internal fake-email approvals, system access and beneficiary-account control.
cases.legal_provisions: IT Act 43; IT Act 66; IT Act 66C; IT Act 66D; IPC 408; IPC 420; IPC 468
cases.disposition: The court found Anubhava Sharma guilty under IT Act 66D and IPC 420, acquitted him on the remaining charged offences, and released him on probation instead of imposing immediate imprisonment.
cases.case_summary: A fictitious motor-broking entity was used to enter an insurance-company business workflow, and fake internal email approvals were recorded in the refund process. The prosecution alleged INR 88,983,100 in refunds to the associated account. The final court found Anubhava Sharma guilty of cheating and cheating by personation but acquitted him on hacking, identity-theft, criminal-breach-of-trust and forgery counts. The judgment contains internal date and header inconsistencies, which are preserved rather than normalized away.
cases.research_notes: The judgment's formal incident period is 1 September 2023 to 26 February 2024. The text states refunds of INR 88,983,100 and elsewhere a witness refers to about INR 110,000,000. The structured loss field uses the specific prosecution figure. The header says 'Accused is acquitted' but the operative order convicts under IPC 420 and IT Act 66D.

cases.court_or_authority: ACJM-06, Rouse Avenue District Courts, New Delhi
cases.impersonated_identity_detail: Bio-Chemic Education Grant Commission falsely projected as a Government of India body
cases.initial_contact_summary: Job seekers encountered BEGC vacancy material presented through websites and Gazette-linked publications as if BEGC were a genuine Government of India organisation.
cases.pretext_summary: BEGC used government-style names, seals, Gazette publications, websites and banking arrangements to create an official appearance and advertised hundreds of posts requiring application fees.

cases.victim_action: For the focal coding example, Shahid Mudassar applied for employment and paid an application fee of INR 200.

actors.relationship_note: Do not transfer Bhupesh Arora's identified human status to the unknown LOXAM operator function.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The bail order records the prosecution allegation and the Court's prima facie view that A1 participated in the WhatsApp digital-arrest threat and obtained money, but it does not provide a transaction/account-control map sufficient to assign a definite financial function.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged participation in the WhatsApp terrorism-pretext digital-arrest interaction and threats that induced repeated online transfers.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source is a bail order and does not reproduce independent WhatsApp provider, telecom, device or beneficiary-account evidence tying the victim-facing identity and payment endpoints to A1.
actors.alternative_explanation: A1 denied participation and alleged false implication; those claims were not finally adjudicated.
actors.relationship_note: Victim-facing function is based on the bail-stage record and must not be read as a final finding of guilt.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The order says A1 acted with the help of A2 and later describes A2 as the main accused who was absconding, but it does not specify A2's exact victim-facing or payment-path conduct.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged assistance/main-accused role in the digital-arrest scheme.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source supplies no name for A2 in the reviewed text and does not detail the specific communications, account control or withdrawals attributable to A2.
actors.alternative_explanation: The phrase main accused is a procedural/prosecution characterization and does not itself establish the function performed.
actors.relationship_note: A2 is kept as a numbered actor cluster rather than treated as an identified human.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The complainant narrative records repeated calls/emails using purported TimesJobs and AECOM identities. The reviewed judgment does not resolve all those victim-facing identities to specific humans.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the staged recruitment pretext, interview/job-offer communications and escalating fee demands.
actors.attribution_limitations: The communications and pretext are detailed, but authorship of each phone/email identity is not mapped to a specific real-world human in the judgment.
actors.relationship_note: Keep separate from petitioners linked mainly through bank and subscriber infrastructure.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The order records multiple beneficiary accounts in Satish Kushwaha's name and traces the complainant's funds through those accounts; it does not identify him as the initial recruiter/caller.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged control of multiple bank accounts through which the job-fraud payments were routed.
actors.attribution_limitations: Bank-account linkage supports a financial role, while the source does not establish that he authored the TimesJobs/AECOM communications or every transaction in the broader network.
actors.alternative_explanation: Account ownership/control can establish a financial endpoint without establishing authorship of the recruitment persona.
actors.relationship_note: Financial role is separate from the unresolved victim-facing recruiter cluster.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The investigation associated a mobile number registered to Abhishek Tiwari with two fraud-linked bank accounts, but the judgment does not establish his control of victim-facing recruitment identities or a complete account-control chain.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged subscriber/account-infrastructure association within the job-fraud network.
actors.attribution_limitations: Subscriber registration and account association are meaningful links but do not substantially establish that he controlled the relevant accounts at the time or delivered the social-engineering interaction.
actors.alternative_explanation: A registered subscriber/account association may reflect a narrower infrastructure role or disputed control.
actors.relationship_note: Do not transfer identified-human status to the unresolved TimesJobs/AECOM operator function.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The Supreme Court order records a defined group of fraudsters impersonating CBI, ED and judicial authorities and displaying forged judicial orders, but it does not identify specific real-world humans or map the payment path.
actors.conduct_assessed: Delivering the digital-arrest communications, forged-order legitimacy theatre and threats that induced INR 10.55 million in transfers.
actors.attribution_limitations: The focal incident and impersonation sequence are clearly recorded, but human identity and operator-specific telecom/device/payment evidence are absent from this procedural order.
actors.relationship_note: Actor cluster is incident-level and should not be read as resolved human attribution.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The source states that an impostor using the name Kaustubh Das presented himself as Prashant Buradkar's authorized representative and obtained a replacement SIM; it does not resolve the impostor's actual human identity.
actors.conduct_assessed: Using a false authorized-representative identity and documents to induce Vodafone to issue/activate a replacement SIM.
actors.attribution_limitations: The replacement request and false representation are documented, but the human behind the identity remains unresolved and the judgment does not map that person to every banking transaction.
actors.relationship_note: Keep distinct from the downstream banking/beneficiary cluster.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The adjudicatory record links the SIM-swap episode to siphoning from the SBI account but does not fully identify or individually assess the humans controlling downstream financial endpoints.
actors.conduct_assessed: Receiving/routing the INR 1.05 million allegedly siphoned after the replacement-SIM event.
actors.attribution_limitations: The financial consequence is documented for liability purposes, but actor-specific criminal attribution for the downstream recipients is not developed in the reviewed judgment.
actors.alternative_explanation: A beneficiary endpoint need not be the same actor who performed the SIM impersonation.
actors.relationship_note: Financial cluster is analytically distinct from the unknown in-person impostor.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The complainant reported joining a WhatsApp group styled as UBS Asset Management and being induced to invest; the judgment does not identify the humans operating that group.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the WhatsApp investment pretext and inducing continued payments under the purported UBS-branded trading scheme.
actors.attribution_limitations: The complaint and court record establish the victim-facing pretext, but no provider/device evidence identifies the human operators.
actors.relationship_note: Keep separate from layered beneficiary accounts and from V-Mart's remote-layer legitimate merchant account.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Police preliminary investigation traced a specific INR 2.2 million subset through successive accounts. The source does not resolve all human controllers or establish knowing participation by every remote-layer account.
actors.conduct_assessed: Receiving and routing a traced subset of the complainant's investment-fraud payments through layered accounts.
actors.attribution_limitations: The payment path is concrete, but the source does not establish knowledge/intent for every account and does not map the full INR 14.8 million reported loss.
actors.alternative_explanation: At remote layers, legitimate merchant/pass-through transactions are possible, as illustrated by V-Mart's account-freeze challenge.
actors.relationship_note: Do not treat V-Mart itself as a fraud actor merely because INR 4,194 reached its collection account.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Victim account describes calls and WhatsApp video impersonating telecom/police authority; humans unresolved.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the phone/WhatsApp digital-arrest pretext and directing victim transfers.
actors.attribution_limitations: No provider/device evidence in the bail order resolves the human operators.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Applicant was alleged to facilitate account opening/money transfers in a wider network; he denied knowing fraud provenance.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged onboarding/account-opening and money-transfer facilitation within downstream network.
actors.attribution_limitations: Applicant-specific link is bail-stage and contested; source does not identify him as the caller or clearly map focal victim funds to him.
actors.alternative_explanation: He described his Jan Seva Kendra work and business arrangement as legitimate and denied knowledge of fraud.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Victim narrative describes bank, Bandra Police and CBI personas using forged official material; individual humans unresolved.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the layered bank/law-enforcement digital-arrest deception and directing payment.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source reconstructs the deception but does not independently resolve the operators.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Co-accused disclosure statements alleged that he collected and passed account/ATM/SIM materials within an account-procurement network.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged collection and forwarding of mule-account materials to downstream coordinators.
actors.attribution_limitations: No focal victim payment entered his own account and he was not alleged to have made the victim-facing calls.
actors.alternative_explanation: He denied deception, beneficiary status and challenged reliance on co-accused disclosures.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Vodafone confirmed a SIM replacement occurred without PNP Polytex consent after a request by a fraudster.
actors.conduct_assessed: Impersonating/posing as an authorized subscriber requester to obtain the replacement SIM.
actors.attribution_limitations: Human identity of the requester is unresolved and the judgment is not a criminal attribution proceeding.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Bank records document 14 unauthorized transfers to seven initially added beneficiaries with broader routing thereafter.
actors.conduct_assessed: Receiving and routing proceeds from the corporate bank-account takeover.
actors.attribution_limitations: The judgment does not individually determine knowledge or criminal guilt of each downstream account controller.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Victim-facing operators used CBI/Mumbai Crime Branch identities, forged warrants and court material.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the digital-arrest deception and directing RTGS transfers.
actors.attribution_limitations: Individual operators remain unresolved in the bail record.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Investigation alleged that routed funds reached the applicant and were converted through crypto/USDT, with chats to co-accused found on his phone.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged downstream receipt/conversion of cyber-fraud proceeds into cryptocurrency.
actors.attribution_limitations: Applicant denied knowing involvement and described crypto activity as legitimate; FSL extraction and further investigation were ongoing.
actors.alternative_explanation: Legitimate pre-existing USD/cryptocurrency conversion business.

actors.function_assignment_basis: WhatsApp/Telegram groups induced the complainant into the high-return Bitcoin scheme; humans unresolved.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating investment-group communications and directing repeated transfers.
actors.attribution_limitations: No independent provider/device attribution identifies the humans behind the groups.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Investigation alleged control/use of a YES Bank account supplied by a co-accused and broader mule-account coordination.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged control/use and circulation of mule-account infrastructure receiving fraud proceeds.
actors.attribution_limitations: Victim did not identify him as the inducer; knowledge/control allegations remained for investigation.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Unknown WhatsApp callers impersonated Maharashtra Police and used a terrorist-funding/Aadhaar pretext.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the digital-arrest threat and directing transfers.
actors.attribution_limitations: No provider/device evidence in the source resolves the callers.

actors.function_assignment_basis: He was the authorized signatory of a first-layer company account that received INR 3,920,280; onward transfers were under investigation.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged control of a first-layer beneficiary account receiving a portion of victim funds.
actors.attribution_limitations: Knowledge and authorization were contested and second-layer investigation remained incomplete.
actors.alternative_explanation: He claimed his phone/account had been compromised and that he had independently reported/frozen it.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Victim received DHL parcel pretext followed by police/Skype impersonation and safe-custody demands.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the DHL-to-police deception and directing transfers.
actors.attribution_limitations: Human operators remain unresolved.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Prosecution alleged he supplied a mule account and received INR 25,000 commission.
actors.conduct_assessed: Allegedly providing a bank account for receipt/routing of fraud proceeds for commission.
actors.attribution_limitations: Bail-stage allegation; source does not link him to victim-facing contact and guilt remained for trial.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Phone/WhatsApp video callers threatened criminal liability, imprisonment and family consequences while isolating the victim.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the digital-arrest coercion and directing repeated transfers.
actors.attribution_limitations: Human operators and accounts are not fully resolved in the bail record.

actors.function_assignment_basis: A first-layer ICICI account of his proprietorship received INR 4.5 million from the victim; investigation records a disputed disclosure statement.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged control of a first-layer beneficiary account receiving part of the proceeds.
actors.attribution_limitations: He denied knowing participation and claimed his account had itself been compromised.
actors.alternative_explanation: Claimed to be a cyber-fraud victim and denied benefiting from the transfer.

actors.function_assignment_basis: WhatsApp/Telegram/portal operators offered rating work, seeded trust with small payout and escalated prepaid tasks.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the task-scam communications, portal and escalating deposit demands.
actors.attribution_limitations: Human identities behind the messaging and portal are unresolved.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Bail order records transfer of alleged scam funds into an account linked to the applicant.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged downstream receipt/handling of victim funds.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source does not establish that he originated the victim-facing WhatsApp/Telegram deception.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Victim describes in-person honeytrap followed by WhatsApp/phone threats and repeated monetary demands.
actors.conduct_assessed: Creating intimate material and using it in repeated reputational/sexual blackmail demands.
actors.attribution_limitations: Multiple aliases/callers are described and human-role mapping is incomplete.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Co-accused statement alleged the intimate video was sent to him and that he participated in conspiracy/demanding money.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged conspiracy/coordination role in the sextortion network.
actors.attribution_limitations: Attribution in this bail order depends materially on co-accused statements and was not finally adjudicated.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Unknown persons impersonated IPS officers and placed the elderly complainant under digital arrest.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the money-laundering digital-arrest deception and directing transfers.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source does not identify the communication platform or resolve the human callers.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Prosecution alleged he handled/transferred INR 9,782,500 and was in contact with co-accused; mastermind allegation arose via co-accused statement.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged downstream coordination and movement of a substantial part of the proceeds.
actors.attribution_limitations: Mastermind attribution relies partly on co-accused statement and does not establish victim-facing conduct.

actors.function_assignment_basis: WhatsApp/Telegram operators induced the complainant to perform investment-based tasks and make transfers.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the task-scam communications and inducement.
actors.attribution_limitations: Human operators remain unresolved.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Investigation linked him to Rapipay agent infrastructure, virtual-account complaints, IP logs, fund flows and co-accused.
actors.conduct_assessed: Alleged facilitation/routing of proceeds through Rapipay/account infrastructure.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source does not establish that he authored the original WhatsApp/Telegram inducement and findings are bail-stage only.
actors.alternative_explanation: He alleged misuse and denied knowing involvement.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Victim testimony, police interception and appellate findings directly support the impersonation, threats and taking of property.
actors.conduct_assessed: Posing as Local Crime Branch officers, threatening a sexual-offence case, assaulting the complainant and demanding a settlement payment.
actors.attribution_limitations: The record strongly supports the conduct of the relevant male accused but does not imply that every person present had the same role.
actors.alternative_explanation: Individual responsibility remains accused-specific within the group.
actors.relationship_note: Separate from the female lure actor because the appellate court treated her alleged coordination differently.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The source supports the request for a lift and sexual proposal, but the appellate court found no sufficient proof that she had pre-arranged the later extortion with the male accused.
actors.conduct_assessed: Requesting a lift and proposing an intimate encounter that preceded the police-impersonation extortion.
actors.attribution_limitations: The appellate court found insufficient evidence of prior association, common intention or conspiracy with the male extortion actors.
actors.alternative_explanation: Her conduct may have been independent rather than part of the extortion plan.
actors.relationship_note: Do not infer conspiracy merely from the temporal sequence.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The report attributes the fraudulent blocking and replacement of the victim's SIM to unknown fraudsters.
actors.conduct_assessed: Obtaining control of the victim's mobile number through a duplicate SIM and enabling e-banking credential generation.
actors.attribution_limitations: No human identity or telecom replacement documentation is reproduced in the public report.
actors.alternative_explanation: A known person or insider could have assisted the replacement process, as police had not ruled that out.
actors.relationship_note: Victim-facing function refers here to the telecom-facing social-engineering step rather than direct contact with the bank customer.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The report documents three transfers and withdrawals in Delhi and West Bengal but does not resolve account control to named humans.
actors.conduct_assessed: Receiving or withdrawing the proceeds generated after the duplicate-SIM takeover.
actors.attribution_limitations: The public report does not show whether the cash-out actors also obtained the duplicate SIM or knew the full scheme.
actors.alternative_explanation: A downstream account or withdrawal actor may have had a narrower role.
actors.relationship_note: Kept separate from the duplicate-SIM operator absent evidence of overlap.

actors.actor_label: Alleged false-profile relationship and blackmail operator
actors.function_assignment_basis: Victim accounts identify one alleged operator as using false Facebook names, relationship grooming and later image-based coercion.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating a false social profile, cultivating trust, obtaining money/jewellery and allegedly using compromising images for blackmail.
actors.attribution_limitations: The public report does not reproduce platform-provider records, seized-device findings or a final judicial determination.
actors.alternative_explanation: The suspect disputed or had not yet been finally adjudicated on the allegations in the source reviewed.
actors.relationship_note: The focal record does not attribute the conduct of other reported victim episodes to this one.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The victim account documents sustained matrimonial, phone, WhatsApp and email interaction with the Benjamin persona.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the prospective-groom identity and cultivating trust and marriage expectations.
actors.attribution_limitations: The public source does not resolve the online persona to a verified human.
actors.alternative_explanation: A separate operator may have handled the persona from the later customs and bank-account stages.
actors.relationship_note: Kept separate from the fake customs/payment layer.

actors.function_assignment_basis: A woman posing as customs staff demanded payments and supplied bank accounts after the romantic persona established trust.
actors.conduct_assessed: Impersonating customs authority and directing the victim to transfer release and certificate charges.
actors.attribution_limitations: The article does not identify the customs caller or prove control of each beneficiary account.
actors.alternative_explanation: The customs caller and account controllers may have been distinct network members.
actors.relationship_note: Downstream layer separated from the matrimonial persona absent proof of common human identity.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The victim described one sustained Facebook persona that solicited personal media and later threatened distribution.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the false romantic identity, soliciting personal media and threatening or carrying out distribution.
actors.attribution_limitations: The claimed identity and foreign residence were not verified; the public report does not contain provider attribution.
actors.alternative_explanation: A single human or more than one person could have controlled the account over time.
actors.relationship_note: No downstream financial actor is coded because the source does not report a payment demand or transfer.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The victim account establishes the matrimonial persona and phone contact, but the source does not resolve that persona to a specific arrested suspect.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the NRI prospective-groom identity and inducing the airport-clearance transfer.
actors.attribution_limitations: No platform-provider attribution to a named human is reported.
actors.alternative_explanation: The profile operator may have been separate from the cash-out participants.
actors.relationship_note: Separated from cash-out actors.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Police linked three arrested suspects to withdrawal of the transferred money through ATM CCTV and the transaction trail.
actors.conduct_assessed: Withdrawing or controlling proceeds sent after the matrimonial deception.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source does not prove which arrested participant, if any, authored the matrimonial communications.
actors.alternative_explanation: Cash-out involvement can be narrower than direct participation in the initial deception.
actors.relationship_note: Do not collapse cash-out attribution into the groom persona without provider evidence.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Facebook and phone interactions delivered the marriage promise and gift pretext.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the prospective-husband identity and setting up the gift/customs payment stage.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source does not resolve the Facebook profile to a verified human.
actors.alternative_explanation: The persona and fake airport caller may have been operated by different people.
actors.relationship_note: Separated from the fake customs/payment layer.

actors.function_assignment_basis: A woman claiming to call from the airport supplied a bank account and directed the payment of purported customs charges.
actors.conduct_assessed: Impersonating airport/customs authority and directing the victim's transfers.
actors.attribution_limitations: No human identity or account-control evidence beyond the victim/police report is reproduced.
actors.alternative_explanation: The receiving-account controller may be distinct from the caller.
actors.relationship_note: Downstream financial layer.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Police linked the threat phone to the accused through call details and reported his admission that he created the scheme.
actors.conduct_assessed: Creating the fake female identity, obtaining photographs, morphing an image and making the extortion demand.
actors.attribution_limitations: Public reporting summarizes but does not reproduce the telecommunications or device evidence.
actors.alternative_explanation: The attribution had not been finally adjudicated in the source reviewed.
actors.relationship_note: Single alleged operator; no separate downstream financial role because no payment was made.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Police attributed the ad, phone trust-building and jewellery scheme to the arrested suspect and reported extensive SIM/jewellery recoveries.
actors.conduct_assessed: Publishing the false matrimonial pretext, cultivating prospective brides by phone and obtaining valuables under a safekeeping story.
actors.attribution_limitations: The news source does not provide victim-specific forensic attribution for every seized item.
actors.alternative_explanation: Some seized material may relate to other reported victims in the alleged series.
actors.relationship_note: Focal conduct is limited to the Hosur complainant.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The woman directly called, arranged the meeting, changed venues and led the victim into the serviced apartment.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the prospective-bride persona and steering the victim to the isolated meeting location.
actors.attribution_limitations: No telecom or platform attribution to a verified human is provided.
actors.alternative_explanation: The name and employment story may have been fabricated.
actors.relationship_note: Distinct from the three unidentified accomplices.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The victim described three men in the serviced apartment who participated in the robbery, PIN demand and threat.
actors.conduct_assessed: Using the pre-arranged meeting to take valuables, obtain an ATM PIN and support the reputational threat.
actors.attribution_limitations: The suspects were unidentified in the report and no downstream ATM use was established.
actors.alternative_explanation: The article does not establish which participant planned the online/telephone pretext.
actors.relationship_note: Group role separated from the woman who initiated the matrimonial contact.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The source describes an online impostor presenting as a UK-based Indian doctor and prospective husband.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the fake suitor identity and establishing trust for the gift/customs payment pretext.
actors.attribution_limitations: The public report does not identify a human controller of the profile.
actors.alternative_explanation: The persona may have been operated by a team rather than one person.
actors.relationship_note: Victim-facing persona layer.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The victim was directed to make payments in the gift/customs stage of the scheme.
actors.conduct_assessed: Receiving or directing the payments generated by the purported overseas gift and customs-clearance pretext.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source does not identify account holders or connect them directly to the suitor persona.
actors.alternative_explanation: Downstream receiving accounts may have been controlled by separate participants.
actors.relationship_note: Financial layer separated from the online persona.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The family interacted for weeks with the fake prospective-groom profile and associated contact number.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the London-groom identity and introducing the surprise-gift pretext.
actors.attribution_limitations: The persona was not resolved to a verified human in the source.
actors.alternative_explanation: A separate actor could have operated the later customs call.
actors.relationship_note: Separated from customs and payment roles.

actors.function_assignment_basis: A caller using the name Namita Sharma threatened a terror-funding case and directed transfers to named accounts.
actors.conduct_assessed: Impersonating customs authority, escalating fear and directing payments.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source does not establish the real identity of the caller or control of the named accounts.
actors.alternative_explanation: Account holders may have been downstream participants rather than the caller.
actors.relationship_note: Downstream authority and payment layer.

actors.actor_label: Convicted Pollachi social-engineering / blackmail operator group
actors.function_assignment_basis: A final trial-court verdict, as reported, convicted all nine defendants after survivor testimony and extensive documentary/digital evidence.
actors.conduct_assessed: Participating in the organised pattern of false friendship, luring, recorded abuse and blackmail, with individual role differences preserved.
actors.attribution_limitations: The news report does not map every social-engineering and blackmail act to each individual defendant.
actors.alternative_explanation: Different defendants had different proved roles and sentence counts.
actors.relationship_note: Group-level actor record avoids overstating identical conduct across all nine defendants.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Police attributed intimate-message social engineering and requests for military information to a fake account associated with Pakistani intelligence activity.
actors.conduct_assessed: Cultivating the soldier through a false romantic/social identity and eliciting confidential military information.
actors.attribution_limitations: The persona was not resolved to a specific human handler in the public source.
actors.alternative_explanation: The account may have been collaboratively operated or supported by multiple handlers.
actors.relationship_note: The arrested soldier is treated as the social-engineering target, not as the victim-facing operator.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Investigators attributed the sustained Facebook/WhatsApp honeytrap and information requests to a female persona linked to Pakistani intelligence.
actors.conduct_assessed: Building intimate trust with the soldiers and eliciting strategic information through social-media channels.
actors.attribution_limitations: The source does not identify the real-world human operator behind the profile.
actors.alternative_explanation: The profile may have been managed by more than one intelligence handler.
actors.relationship_note: The soldiers are targets of the social-engineering interaction even though they were themselves under investigation.

actors.function_assignment_basis: Police identified the arrested suspect as the person allegedly using the Ravirajsinh identity and carrying out the job-promise and blackmail sequence.
actors.conduct_assessed: Using a false OLX-linked identity, cultivating trust, promising a police job and using recorded material to obtain money.
actors.attribution_limitations: The public source does not reproduce platform or device forensic evidence and no final judgment is cited.
actors.alternative_explanation: Police attribution remained subject to investigation and trial.
actors.relationship_note: Single alleged operator record; no separate beneficiary-account layer is established.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The High Court said case-diary material prima facie implicated the applicant in allegations of defrauding medical aspirants through false admission promises.
actors.conduct_assessed: Offering or facilitating purported SMIMS medical admission through personation/forged-material allegations.
actors.attribution_limitations: Bail-stage prima facie material is not a final finding of guilt and the detailed victim evidence is not reproduced.
actors.alternative_explanation: The applicant denied involvement and said he was not named in the FIR.
actors.relationship_note: Attribution is intentionally limited to the conduct assessed at bail stage.

actors.function_assignment_basis: The victim described the fake Birmingham-businessman profile and direct release-payment request after the airport call.
actors.conduct_assessed: Operating the prospective-groom identity and inducing the victim to finance a fabricated airport detention.

sources.title: Facebook fake-account fraud and blackmail allegations involving women in Agra

sources.title: Conmen posing as Mr Right cheat women of lakhs online

sources.title: Friendship on Facebook ends in blackmail plot against woman
sources.claim_scope: Victim complaint and police account of the Aniket Sharma persona, marriage promise, intimate-media solicitation, later threats and FIR.
sources.notes: The operator's real-world identity was unresolved at publication.

sources.title: West Bengal girl duped of lakhs on false marriage promise, 3 Nigerians arrested

sources.title: Facebook friend dupes woman of Rs 30 lakh after marriage promise
sources.claim_scope: Police and victim account of Facebook relationship grooming, marriage promise, fake diamond gift, airport/customs caller, bank transfer and FIR.
sources.notes: The identities behind the Facebook and airport personas were unresolved in the report.

sources.title: Youth poses as girl to blackmail uncle's pal
sources.claim_scope: Police-sourced reconstruction of fake female persona, target selection, morphed images, extortion demand, call-detail tracing and arrest.
sources.notes: The underlying platform records and CDRs are not reproduced.

sources.title: 59-yr-old Chennai man used fake matrimonial ad to cheat over 20 women

sources.notes: The article also describes a broader serial pattern. Atlas does not aggregate all reported victims into one loss figure.

sources.title: Man robbed of phone, gold by 'bride', 3 others
sources.claim_scope: Victim complaint and police account of the prospective-bride persona, venue changes, serviced-apartment isolation, robbery, PIN disclosure and blackmail threat.
sources.notes: The suspects' real identities were unresolved at publication.

sources.title: 4 months, 3,000 cases and Rs 32 crore: Cyber crooks continue to make merry in IT hub
sources.claim_scope: City cybercrime report containing a specific 39-year-old Jayanagar victim example involving a fake UK doctor on a marriage portal and INR 33 lakh loss.
sources.notes: The article gives less procedural detail than a case-specific court or police source; operator identity is unresolved.

sources.title: Fraudsters pose as prospective groom, customs official to dupe doctor's family of over Rs 4 lakh
sources.claim_scope: Police-sourced reconstruction of fake matrimonial profile, London-groom persona, gift pretext, fake customs/terror-funding threat, transfers and FIR.
sources.notes: Operator identities and account control remained matters for investigation.

sources.title: All nine guilty in 2019 Pollachi sexual abuse case, sentenced to life imprisonment
sources.claim_scope: Verdict report establishing the false-friendship, abuse, recording and blackmail pattern and the conviction/life sentences of all nine accused.
sources.notes: The article is a journalistic summary of the judgment; it does not reproduce the full role-by-role evidentiary record.

sources.title: Honey-trapped on social media, jawan leaks secret Army information to ISI
sources.claim_scope: Police-sourced report describing the fake Anika Chopra profile, intimate-message honeytrap, military-information requests, arrest and alleged Pakistani intelligence linkage.

sources.title: Honey-trapped soldiers nabbed in Rajasthan for leaking information to ISI agent

sources.title: State by Cyber Crime P.S. v. Nikhil Dhingra & Anr., 6 March 2015
sources.court_or_body: I Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore
sources.claim_scope: Final criminal trial reconstructing a 2009 ICICI phishing email, INR 400,000 transfer, IP evidence, beneficiary accounts, seized laptop/mobile material and Truth Lab forensic findings before acquitting the two tried accused.
sources.notes: T1 final judgment. The court distinguished the underlying phishing event from proof that the two tried accused operated the phishing or transaction infrastructure.

sources.title: State by Cyber Crime v. Pravardhan, 28 April 2016
sources.court_or_body: I Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore
sources.claim_scope: Final criminal trial describing a 2013 fake Rockline Venkatesh Facebook profile, acting-opportunity messages and alleged harassment; the accused was acquitted after the complainant turned hostile and operator identity was not established.
sources.notes: T1 final judgment. No financial loss is coded.

sources.title: Cyber Crime Police Station v. Harish S.R., 28 March 2026
sources.court_or_body: XLV Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru
sources.claim_scope: Final criminal judgment concerning a 2017 duplicate-SIM and OTP-enabled account-takeover allegation, seized mobile evidence, missing FSL result and failures to establish the accused-device-recipient-account chain.
sources.notes: T1 final judgment. financial_loss_inr remains blank because the judgment does not state a reliable focal amount.

sources.title: State by R.T. Nagar Police Station v. Rakesh Kumar K.A. & Anr., 18 July 2025
sources.court_or_body: VIII Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City
sources.claim_scope: Final criminal judgment reconstructing an in-person lead-management service pretext, phone/app access, card handling and INR 63,000 in unauthorized debits; both accused were acquitted because the digital and financial linkage was not proved.
sources.notes: T1 final judgment. Bank/card statements were available, but the relevant device, app, wallet and beneficiary evidence was not secured.

sources.title: State by Kadugondanahalli Police Station v. Harshiya Khanam, 16 March 2021
sources.court_or_body: I Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru
sources.claim_scope: Final criminal trial describing a fake Facebook romance persona, alleged INR 1,400,000 in repeated transfers, bank/CCTV/CDR evidence and the acquittal of accused No.2 after the court found the actor-specific financial and communication linkage unproved.
sources.notes: The case against accused No.1 Sherkhan had been split up. The court found that Facebook records were not investigated, no relevant CDR linked accused No.2 to the complainant, and CCTV evidence was not proved in accordance with law.

sources.claim_scope: Final criminal trial concerning a fictitious insurance-lead entity, fake email approvals, corporate refund transfers and the conviction of Anubhava Sharma under IPC 420 and IT Act 66D.
